question: Can exactly represented FP32 unit counts remove the int64 atomic penalty while preserving graph capture and the compact optimizer gate?
exactness_argument: Every layer contains at most 2,359,296 scalar assignments, below 2^24.
Starting from zero, every addition of FP32 one yields an exactly represented integer throughout this range, independent of atomic order.
The reference immediately casts int64 counts to FP32 before division; therefore the candidate supplies the identical FP32 divisor for every fixed assignment.
frozen_intervention: Change only the graph-safe count accumulator and unit source from int64 to FP32.
Retain reference torch.searchsorted, separate FP32 sum index_add, static torch.where centroid update, sorting, final assignment, and selected group sizes 12,12,24,12,24,12,12.
Capture and retain all seven role graphs in a shared graph pool; timed replay includes input and durable output copies.
Standalone no-training oracle only; do not edit MuonPairVQ.

decision_rule.all_gates_pass: Preregister a two-phase optimizer integration with exact state, independent replay, memory, and >=20% MFU gates; do not automatically train.
